notes: A 45-second round timer, a lobby everyone waits in, an automatic teleport into a match area and a scored finish is Party & Casual's Minigame almost line for line, so it leads; Obby & Platformer is named second only because the shaft is an obstacle course and Party & Casual has no row for moving blocks or contact hazards, and its genre-wide P6 does not follow it into a mix it did not lead. Shape stays the preset's space-staged: the floating lobby and the glass shaft are separate areas joined by a teleport rather than one continuous surface, and nothing in the prompt asks for them to be joined, so the P4 stands. I added CHECK on top because the play space is a freefall volume rather than a ground plane — obstacles are stacked at many heights over the same footprint, so the volume genuinely self-occludes — and I kept the answer's single straight shaft with the trophy visible through the glass. Dropped two preset options: the leaderboard wall, which the prompt never asks for while specifying the lobby floor in detail, and the spectator area, which is contradicted outright since players who hit a hazard respawn in the lobby; the golden trophy on the safe floor is winner-zone, and the coin-bought falling speeds and gravity coils sit on the lobby's upgrade pads as part of social-hub.
